correctness.rationale: A de Bruijn necklace of order five is exactly an Eulerian circuit of the four-bit de Bruijn digraph, uniquely rooted at its sole 00000 edge. The complete \(32\)-edge DFS visits all and only such circuits; the built-in five-factor assertion and collision assertion check bijection. For each accepted circuit, sorting the 32 literal cyclic rotations defines the BWT and yields its linear run number. The independent full \(2^{16}\) `01`/`10`-block enumeration uses the classical BWT-pair characterization and exact LF single-32-cycle criterion; all \(2048\) accepted BWT strings agree as sets between approaches, and their histograms independently agree. The included verify.py was executed from the actual locally prepared file, finishing VERIFY_OK with six cells 38,426,840,608,130,6. Finite exhaustive proof only: no infinite-order claim or extrapolation.

evidence: Mantaci et al. (2017), Theorem 5.2, DOI 10.1016/j.tcs.2017.07.015, provides a general lower bound \(2^{n-1}+2\) and upper bound \(2^n-2\) on BWT runs for binary de Bruijn words; at order five these are 18 and 30.
Their bound includes all cycles, but the inspected proof does not enumerate how many cycles take each run number, nor show the sharper minimum \(20\) for \(n=5\).
The unrestricted total number of de Bruijn cycles is 2048, known from classical results and also verified, but an unweighted total does not imply any of the six refined histogram cells.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier all-order statement dominates the scope but not the conclusion: its lower bound of 18 is weaker than the exact minimum 20; its upper bound does not supply attainment or multiplicity. The general BWT characterizations imply a finite algorithm but not the computed exact distribution without the separate enumeration.

originality.rationale: Higgins (2012) provides the BWT permutation-block characterization but not the run-refined order-five census. Mantaci et al. (2017), Theorem 5.2, give only an order-five run interval \(18\) through \(30\), whereas exhaustive analysis yields minimum 20 and six exact multiplicities. Fici and Gabory (2025) give BWT-Hamiltonian-cycle descriptions and unrefined totals; the relevant sections contain no order-five run spectrum. Liptak and Parmigiani (2024) present a BWT-based generation algorithm, not an exact complete run table in the accessible author presentation. Indexed mathematical-record and literature queries for the exact coefficients, extrema, equivalent LF transition-statistics and wider domination found no covering published result, but search nonhits are not proofs of novelty. A related 2024 complete chapter remained inaccessible, so previously unindexed equivalence remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A prior unindexed exact order-five BWT histogram or alternative LF transition-count table may already exist; finite search cannot prove its global absence.
The full 2024 Lipták–Parmigiani chapter was not accessed; available author presentation and abstract were inspected but may omit a relevant appendix.
The result is a motivated exact finite classification, not a general formula over all de Bruijn orders or a claim about absolute compressed bit count.

value.rationale: Full de Bruijn cycles are canonical shortest exhaustive 5-mer datasets, and cyclic BWT run count is a standard structural statistic used to evaluate run-length-based text indexing. The exact distribution over every one of 2048 order-five cycles, including a sharpened attainable minimum 20 and its 38 realizers, distinguishes which universal cycles are most/least run-friendly; the 6 exact multiplicity cells, mean, and variance give reproducible benchmarks for algorithms generating or choosing such cycles. This is a natural complete finite parameter value; no unsupported infinite or downstream theorem is required. The verified five-bit order is nonarbitrary as a complete natural family and a substantial nontrivial enumeration compared with earlier orders. Limits: significance is finite and BWT run count does not equal total encoded bits.
